nodes.content: Design a distributed scheduler for preemptible gang jobs that reconciles tenant fairness, placement constraints, and recovery from scheduler partitions.
requirements: Prevent conflicting resource assignments during partitions, including stale schedulers and partially completed gang reservations.
After connectivity stabilizes, restore scheduling progress within 30 seconds while preventing starvation under feasible demand.

nodes.content: Use quorum-committed atomic gang leases expiring within ten seconds, worker-enforced epoch fencing, placement-aware deficit scheduling, preemption, and five-second reconciliation.
How can workers release orphaned tentative gang holds without accepting conflicting leases from a stale scheduler?
Ten-second uncommitted-hold expiry and worker-verified epoch-fenced quorum commits yield zero conflicting assignments in partition tests.
Specify quorum-certified prepare/commit, worker-enforced epoch fencing, and ten-second hold expiry; test abandoned prepares and stale schedulers under partitions.
Run PartitionBench-1k with 1,000 randomized partitions, abandoned gang prepares, epoch changes, and delayed commits; measure conflicts and hold-release latency.
PartitionBench-1k found one conflicting assignment when a worker accepted an epoch-8 lease before confirming epoch-7 process termination.
Ten-second tentative-hold expiry plus worker-confirmed old-epoch process termination before lease activation yields zero conflicts in PartitionBench-1k.
Require workers to confirm old-epoch process termination before activating new leases; rerun PartitionBench-1k and measure conflicts and hold-release latency.
PartitionBench-1k rerun recorded zero conflicting assignments across 1,000 partitions and 9.8-second p99 orphan-hold release after worker-confirmed termination.
Adopt worker-confirmed old-epoch process termination before new lease activation; it eliminated the stale-process conflict observed in PartitionBench-1k.
Run GangCrash-500, crashing coordinators after each gang prepare and commit message; measure partial activations and orphan-hold release latency.
GangCrash-500 report records 12 partial gang activations across 500 coordinator crashes and 9.9-second p99 orphan-hold release.
How can workers prevent partial gang activation after a coordinator crash while releasing orphaned holds within ten seconds?
Use quorum-backed gang activation barriers and placement-feasible tenant deficit queues with aging, triggering preemption on reconnection.
Implement fenced quorum gang barriers and placement-aware aging deficit queues; test zero conflicts, starvation, and 30-second recovery under partitions.
Implement fenced, quorum-logged gang-ready certificates and worker start barriers with timeout rollback; retest GangCrash-500's 12 partial-activation cases.
GangBarrier v1 adds quorum-logged all-worker readiness certificates, fenced start tokens, and ten-second rollback of incomplete reservations.
Run PartitionBench-1k and FairGang-200 with GangBarrier v1; measure conflicts, orphan-hold release, partial activations, feasible-tenant starvation, and 30-second recovery compliance.
PartitionBench-1k/FairGang-200 recorded zero conflicts or partial activations, 24-second p99 recovery, and all feasible tenants scheduled within 120 seconds.
Adopt GangBarrier v1 with worker-confirmed epoch fencing and aging deficit queues: zero conflicts or partial activations; 24-second p99 recovery.
How should aging deficit queues bypass placement-infeasible head-of-line gangs without consuming tenant credits or starving smaller feasible gangs?
Skip placement-infeasible gangs without charging deficits; age feasible alternatives, keeping continuously feasible small-gang wait below 120 seconds on FairGang-200.
Inject infeasible head-of-line gangs into FairGang-200; compare credit charging versus skipping, measuring continuously feasible small-gang wait against 120 seconds.
Reconcile quorum-logged leases against worker inventories on reconnection, then preempt bounded batches and resume gang placement within 30 seconds.
How can quorum-log and worker-inventory reconciliation identify stale leases and orphaned holds without exceeding 30-second recovery?
Inject 5,000 stale leases into PartitionBench-1k reconnects; reconcile quorum logs against worker inventories, measuring conflicts and p99 scheduling recovery.
FairGang-200: skipping yielded 147-second continuously feasible small-gang waits versus 183 seconds charging; PartitionBench-1k: zero conflicts, 28-second p99 recovery.
Quorum-log fencing and worker-inventory reconciliation keep p99 recovery below 30 seconds despite 5,000 stale leases, with zero conflicts.
Repeat PartitionBench-1k with 5,000 stale leases, delayed worker inventories, and coordinator failover; measure conflicts and p99 recovery.
PartitionBench-1k with delayed inventories and coordinator failover recorded zero conflicts but 41-second p99 recovery across 5,000 stale leases.
Shard-checkpointed parallel reconciliation schedules only verified workers, yielding zero conflicts and sub-30-second p99 recovery despite delayed inventories and failover.
Test 32-shard checkpointed reconciliation and verified-worker scheduling in PartitionBench-1k with delayed inventories and failover; measure conflicts and p99 recovery.
PartitionBench-1k with 32 reconciliation shards recorded zero conflicts and 26-second p99 recovery under delayed inventories and failover.
Stress 32-shard reconciliation with delayed inventories and repeated failovers in PartitionBench-1k; measure conflicting assignments and p99 recovery.
PartitionBench-1k with repeated failovers recorded zero conflicts but 38-second p99 recovery, exceeding the 30-second target.
How can reconciliation shards survive repeated failovers without exceeding 30-second recovery or scheduling unverified workers?
Quorum-persisted shard cursors and epoch-fenced handoff avoid repeated-failover rescans, yielding zero conflicts and sub-30-second p99 recovery.
Compare baseline 32-shard reconciliation against quorum-persisted cursors and epoch-fenced handoff under repeated failovers; measure p99 recovery and conflicts.
PartitionBench-1k: single-failover baseline p99 recovery was 26 seconds; repeated-failover baseline took 38 versus persisted-cursor 35 seconds; zero conflicts throughout.
Retain verified-worker 32-shard reconciliation for single failovers (26-second p99); defer broader rollout because repeated-failover recovery remains 35 seconds.
Which remaining reconciliation phase causes 35-second p99 recovery despite persisted cursors during repeated failovers?
Worker-inventory revalidation consumes at least 10 seconds of repeated-failover 35-second p99 recovery, exceeding shard-cursor replay time.
Instrument PartitionBench-1k repeated-failover recovery with per-phase spans for worker-inventory revalidation, shard replay, epoch handoff, and gang restart.
PartitionBench-1k: inventory revalidation took 14 seconds versus 4 seconds for shard replay in 35-second p99 repeated-failover recoveries.
Prioritize parallel worker-inventory revalidation while retaining verified-worker gating; defer repeated-failover rollout until p99 recovery falls below 30 seconds.
Parallelize epoch-bound worker-inventory attestations across 32 shards, admitting only verified workers and retaining quorum-backed gang barriers.
Implement parallel epoch-bound inventory attestations with fenced gang barriers and aging deficits; test conflicts, feasible-tenant starvation, and 30-second failover recovery.
Integrate 32-shard parallel inventory attestations with GangBarrier v1, gating gang starts on fresh worker-epoch certificates.
AttestGate v1 adds 32-shard epoch-bound inventory attestations and rejects gang-start tokens lacking fresh certificates for every reserved worker.
Run PartitionBench-1k repeated failovers and FairGang-200 infeasible-head cases with AttestGate v1; measure conflicts, partial activations, p99 recovery, and feasible-tenant waits.
PartitionBench-1k: zero conflicts or partial activations, 27-second p99 repeated-failover recovery; FairGang-200: 147-second continuously feasible small-gang wait.
Adopt AttestGate v1 for 27-second p99 repeated-failover recovery without conflicts; retain aging queues while investigating 147-second small-gang waits.
Use placement-feasible backfill and tenant-credit-triggered preemption after 90 seconds, retaining AttestGate's fenced gang activation.
Add credit-preserving feasible backfill and 90-second preemption; evaluate tenant waits, gang safety, and 30-second partition recovery.
Implement placement-feasible backfill and 90-second credit-triggered preemption atop AttestGate v1, charging deficits only after certified gang activation.
FairBackfill v1 skips infeasible gang heads, preserves tenant credits until certified activation, and preempts lower-credit occupants after 90 seconds.
Run FairGang-200 infeasible-head and PartitionBench-1k repeated-failover cases with FairBackfill v1; measure feasible waits, conflicts, and p99 recovery.
FairGang-200 feasible small-gang wait fell from 147 to 108 seconds; PartitionBench-1k recorded zero conflicts and 28-second p99 recovery.
Adopt FairBackfill with worker-fenced GangBarrier and parallel-attestation AttestGate: zero conflicts, 108-second feasible wait, 28-second p99 recovery.
